stories.title: The first self-driving vehicle on Mars has proven to be a smashing success
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Perseverance rover on Mars has demonstrated high levels of autonomy.
Approximately 90% of the distance driven by the rover has been autonomous.
This marks a significant milestone in autonomous systems development for extraterrestrial exploration.

stories.title: DeepMind’s hurricane breakthrough has surprised weather scientists
stories.author: Victoria Turk, wired.com
bullet_points: DeepMind has achieved a significant breakthrough in weather prediction using AI.
The open-source WeatherNext model demonstrates high accuracy even with lower-resolution weather data.
This development is surprising to established weather scientists, suggesting a major advance in climate modeling.

stories.title: DeepMind's WeatherNext model achieves breakthrough forecasting cyclones
stories.author: bhavansig
bullet_points: DeepMind has developed a new model named WeatherNext.
The model demonstrates a significant breakthrough in forecasting cyclones.
This represents a major application of advanced AI/ML in climate science and meteorology.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer community of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance using Gemma 4 saw up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to faster response times and higher quality model outputs.
The update also results in reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware, enhancing privacy and control.
It features built-in support for Ollama, leveraging existing local LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for enhanced performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware.
The feature is currently available in preview, signaling a push for optimized local AI on Apple devices.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The tool aims to bring powerful AI capabilities directly onto the user's personal device.

stories.title: Judge rules Meta caused "public nuisance" and must fund mental health treatment
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A New Mexico judge ruled that Meta caused a 'public nuisance' related to its platforms.
The ruling mandates that Meta fund a $567 million initiative to address youth mental health.
This case represents a significant legal action linking social media platforms to public health crises.

stories.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
stories.author: Nuno Vasconcelos
bullet_points: Introduces a novel method for On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPD/OSPD) in LLMs.
Addresses the limitation of existing methods that require external supervision (ground-truth, environmental feedback).
Achieves self-distillation solely using the model's own generations via internal consistency.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of local LLM orchestration tools by adding advanced reasoning and information retrieval features.

stories.title: An Amazon data center could have the worst polluting power plant in the country
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Amazon is investing in a new power plant in West Texas to support its data center expansion.
The planned gas-burning power plant could become one of the largest single sources of greenhouse gas emissions in the US.
The story highlights the environmental impact associated with large-scale tech infrastructure development.

stories.title: Europe's free satellite service just made it easier to track wildfires
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Copernicus Browser has been updated to include wildfire visualization capabilities.
The update addresses the increasing severity of the current wildfire season in Europe.
The service leverages existing free satellite data to aid in wildfire tracking and monitoring.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark to test selective context preference.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes 39-45% of data scientists' time.
It focuses specifically on heart failure, a major health issue requiring integration of fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by offering better automation and evidence traceability.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional evaluations by providing a certified anytime-valid stopping condition.
Claims to reduce evaluation costs by a factor of 74 compared to existing methods while maintaining statistical guarantees.

stories.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: Existing video language models struggle with precise event bookkeeping (counting, timing) in real-world scenarios.
Current benchmarks are flawed because they either lack control (real-world clips) or lack auditing capability (programmatic benchmarks).
The research proposes 'trace-grounded parametric profiling' to accurately audit and count specific events in controlled video tasks.

stories.title: Challenges in Evaluating Explanation Methods for Static and Evolving Data
stories.author: Jerzy Stefanowski
bullet_points: The paper addresses critical evaluation limitations within Explainable AI (XAI), particularly concerning insufficient testing methodologies.
It demonstrates practical challenges using the DetoxAI system for bias detection and concept unlearning in image recognition.
The research explores adapting explanation methods, such as counterfactuals, to handle concept drift in evolving data streams.

stories.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
stories.author: Juanzi Li
bullet_points: Introduces TRAJDEBUG, a method designed to trace the error lifecycle in long-horizon agent trajectories.
Addresses a key challenge in LLM-based agentic systems: identifying the earliest critical error causing final failure in complex, long sequences.
Highlights the difficulty of error detection due to scattered evidence across distant instructions and observations in long trajectories.

stories.title: Tytan: Interactive Neurosymbolic Construction of Analytic Semantic Schemas from Relational Data
stories.author: Kristian J. Hammond
bullet_points: Introduces TYTAN, a system designed to automatically construct analytic semantic schemas from relational data.
Addresses the 'knowledge-acquisition bottleneck' where data understanding (entity types, measures, relationships) is currently done manually.
Aims to improve scalability and reduce dependency on data experts for non-technical users in data analysis tools.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of large language models (LLMs) to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark designed to test conditional reasoning under various context conditions.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes a large portion of data scientists' time.
It focuses specifically on heart failure, a condition requiring complex integration of fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by offering more automated and evidence-linked feature engineering.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional agent evaluation by allowing stopping as soon as sufficient evidence is gathered.
Provides a mathematical guarantee that the evaluation's confidence level remains valid even with early stopping.

stories.title: CalibForge: Adversarial Solver Calibration for Scaling Learnable Terminal Tasks
stories.author: Kai Jia
bullet_points: Introduces CalibForge, an autonomous system for synthesizing terminal tasks in reinforcement learning.
The system uses adversarial solver calibration to ensure tasks are appropriately challenging for learning, going beyond simple solvability.
Addresses the gap where executable task validation does not account for how a task behaves relative to a specific solver setting.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in LLM Reinforcement Learning (RL) by focusing on Generative Reward Models (GRMs).
The core problem identified is the incompatibility between GRMs' comparative nature and the scalar scoring required by standard RL algorithms.
The authors propose a novel method (RRC) to bridge this gap, enabling the practical application of GRMs in RL.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in agentic systems is heavily dependent on the surrounding 'harness' (prompts, tools, orchestration, etc.), not just the model weights.
The paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, a framework for evaluating automated harness optimization—the use of AI to iteratively improve the surrounding system components.
A key gap in the current research is the lack of a common protocol for measuring and comparing these harness optimization techniques.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simply training models to ignore context.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark designed to test context reliability under various conditions.

stories.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
stories.author: Vamse Kumar Subbiah
bullet_points: The paper investigates programmatic tool calling (PTC) as an evolution of LLM tool use, moving beyond rigid JSON calls to allow for natural scripting and chaining.
PTC enables LLMs to function as more capable agents that can act beyond their initial training data, especially when code-capable.
The research addresses a gap in current literature by empirically comparing PTC against native JSON tool calling on established benchmarks under real-world conditions.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a new method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional evaluation methods by allowing for 'Anytime-Valid Stopping'.
Claims to achieve 74x cost reduction in agent evaluation while maintaining statistical guarantees.

stories.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
stories.author: Shujian Huang
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of multilingual reasoning transfer in Large Language Models (LLMs), particularly for low-resource languages.
It introduces RP-OPSD, a novel method that enhances On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) by incorporating a Reasoning-Pivot guide.
The core contribution is explicitly prioritizing reasoning signals during distillation to improve cross-lingual transfer capabilities.

stories.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
stories.author: Abigail Goldsteen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of poor quality in existing benchmarks used to evaluate conversational agents.
It introduces a novel, reference-free framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to assess benchmark quality.
The framework provides actionable diagnostics regarding benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage.

stories.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
stories.author: Tianyong Hao
bullet_points: LLMs are being tested on a complex, rule-intensive task: reviewing national standard documents (e.g., China GB/T standards).
The research highlights a gap in current LLM benchmarks, which often focus on domain knowledge rather than strict adherence to explicit rules.
The study aims to evaluate and enhance LLMs' ability to handle lengthy, highly structured documents requiring consistency in terminology and scope.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap between generative reward models (used in ranking) and their application in Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The core problem identified is the mismatch between the comparative nature of generative reward models and the scalar scoring required by existing RL algorithms.
The authors propose a novel method (RRC) to bridge this gap, unlocking the potential of generative reward models in LLM RL.

stories.title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations
stories.author: Tabarakul Hazarika
bullet_points: The paper critiques the standard 'chunk-embed-top-k' approach for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over long documents.
It argues this standard method is structurally unsound for complex, data-heavy documents like financial statements and regulatory reports.
The authors propose replacing black-box retrieval with more interpretable, agentic operations to handle dense, repetitive content.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The focus shifts from just LLM weights to the 'harness' (prompts, tools, orchestration) in agentic systems.
Automated harness optimization—AI-guided improvement of the surrounding system—is identified as a critical, yet challenging, area.
The research highlights a lack of a common protocol for measuring and evaluating these complex LLM harnesses.

stories.title: How to Build AI Evals for Tool-Calling Agents
stories.author: dhanushreddy29
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for robust evaluation methods (AI Evals) in modern LLM applications.
Focuses specifically on the challenge of testing and validating 'Tool-Calling Agents,' a key area in agentic AI.
Highlights the industry problem of over-reliance on unverified or superficial model performance scores.

stories.title: Building ScamLens AI: My Exploration of Artificial Intelligence in Phishing and Social Engineering Detection
stories.author: zain_abuzaid_9f0dd065b56d
bullet_points: The article details the development process of 'ScamLens AI,' an AI tool.
The focus of the project is on detecting phishing and social engineering attacks.
It serves as an exploration into applying AI/ML techniques to cybersecurity threats.
